manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Stack the three bowls on the table.

Task description: The objects are the three light-green bowls scattered on the left side of the table. Stack them vertically into one nested pile.

Success criteria: Pick up and move the bowls to stack all three, with the bottom of the top bowl nested in and supported by the opening of the lower bowl. The complete stack must remain stable on the table.

## Execution tips

- Choose a wall section near the bowl's upper rim, away from the neighboring bowl and with ample outer clearance. Grip with one finger inside and one outside, contacting the wall rather than only the thin edge.
- Set the opening for bowl-wall thickness and entry clearance, confirming the fingers lie inside and outside the wall before closing. Make a small test lift and watch for sliding rather than mistaking image overlap for a secure grasp.
- The three bowls are close together. During lateral transport, keep both the bowl bottom and fingers above neighboring rims, and adjust the pose where there is clearance above to reduce the risk of brushing adjacent bowls.
- While nesting, keep the bowl opening roughly up, align its bottom inside the lower bowl opening, and lower slightly. If one side contacts the rim first or the bowl tilts, raise it slightly and adjust instead of continuing to push down and risking a tip-over.
- During lowering, watch clearance between the outside finger and lower bowl rim. Release once the held bowl is reliably supported and before the fingers become trapped, then withdraw upward to avoid an airborne drop or lifting the lower bowl during withdrawal.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill, read the specified manual, and start this authorized real-robot episode, acting on live observations. When finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode and report my observation-based assessment and the recording directory.

I have read the manual and both live image streams. The three bowls are spread apart, and the tool allows only the right arm. I am adjusting the gripper pose at height, then will align with the bowl wall and confirm the grasp with a small test lift.

The orientation adjustment hit a controller joint limit, and the tool returned a recoverable rejection. The arm moved partly. I will use the returned actual pose to choose a lower approach position and continue adjusting within this episode.
The measured gripper opening is approximately 34.7 mm and it is aligning with the left bowl's outer rim. Near the rim, I will move no more than 1 cm per step and reobserve finger-to-wall positions.

The left bowl rose during a small test lift, but the measured gap is still narrowing, so grasp stability needs confirmation. I will continue small lifts and observe, transporting laterally only once it stops sliding relative to the gripper.

The first bowl has left the table, and the grasp gap is stable at about 4.5 mm. The bowl is slightly tilted; I will lift it higher to ensure its base clears the adjacent bowl rim before moving it farther.
The first bowl has been moved above the bowl behind it. Next I will lower gradually and check alignment between its base and the lower bowl opening, then release once it is supported.

From the image, the lower part of the upper bowl has entered the rear bowl's opening, and the lower bowl remains upright. I will open the gripper slightly to let the upper bowl settle, then withdraw and check that the two bowls are nested.
The two bowls are nested and stable; withdrawing the gripper did not lift the upper bowl. I am now approaching the remaining third bowl at the front, preparing to place it on the stack.
The third bowl wall is visible between the gripper fingers, and there is still vertical clearance. I will open the gripper, lower in stages, and repeat the test lift to check.

The gripper is descending in small steps along the third bowl’s side wall, and both the bowl and completed two-bowl stack remain in place. Alignment is currently good; next I will close the gripper and test-lift.
The third bowl has lifted with the gripper, and the grasp opening has converged to about 4.9 mm. I will confirm stability, raise it, and move above the two bowls already stacked.

The grasp on the third bowl remains stable, and it is moving toward the two-bowl stack. Near the target I will lower in small steps again, check support and finger clearance, then release and withdraw.
The third bowl is aligned with the stack and is gradually entering the top bowl opening. The two lower bowls remain upright, with no visible movement.

After release, all three bowls are nested in one stack, with no visible tipping or sliding apart. I will raise the gripper, confirm stack stability, then end this episode; final success remains for the on-site operator to confirm.
